newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian business optimism up again - survey.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian business optimism up again - survey.

text.p: Business optimism has improved across Australia in the December quarter, continuing the improvement of the previous two quarters, according to a survey by business consultants Dun and Bradstreet (D&B).

"Business optimism in Australia has continued to rise with expectations for growth in orders and sales showing further improvements," said Michael Stensland, D&B Vice-President and area manager for Australia, New Zealand, ASEAN and India region.

"The latest D&B survey indicates a mild recovery in the rate of growth of the Australian economy in the second-half of 1996," Stensland said. However, he said concerns about profits and employment growth remained.
The survey showed that inflation expectations were at their lowest for four years, but capital investment remained flat.
"The static overall selling prices expectations confirms a continuation of low inflation in Australia," said Duncan Ironmonger, economic consultant for D&B.

"Maufacturing executives continue to reduce expectations for raising their expectations for raising their selling prices and although retail executives had raised their price expectations, wholesales had lowered their's," Ironmonger said.

Expectations for growth in capital investement have increased a little from the low point of the March quarter, but were still restrained in line with the low expectations for growth in profits, the survey showed.
"The outlook for growth in profits is still weak, particularly in the distribution and durables manufacturing sectors," Ironmonger said.

The survey showed actual profits results far below expectations. For retailers, the net balance of actual results has been negative for six quarters. For durables manufacturers the situation has been negative for three quarters.
The survey showed employment expectations for the third and fourth quarters indicated that employment would continue to grow slowly over the next six months.
The survey of about 900 business owners and senior executives from major industry sectors was conducted in September.
